## 2. The decisions that need your verdict

### Look

1. **THE KEPT WORLD as the film's spine** — every surface is a document of its keeping, drawn and
   repainted by one goblin over years, and the freeze is when you are allowed to read the file.
   Chosen over a drafting-table reading and a travelling-seam reading. It is what makes "I've built
   worlds for your DM for years" a conclusion you have already verified rather than a claim.
2. **The goblin's cloak goes slate `#2E3742`** — he was measured within 0.02 luma of the trees
   behind him, so the poster had no subject. His colour moves to sage skin and two amber eyes.
3. **The painted tree crowns lighten.** New, forced by the failed verify: the cloak cannot reach the
   required separation from its own side even at its darkest legal value. He owns the darkest
   committed value, so the world lightens around him. *This changes every exterior stage and is the
   single decision I would most like your eye on.*
4. **Snow becomes reserved paper; water becomes bare paper with a drawn edge.** Both remove work and
   raise quality, and they retire the hatched water in `world.ts` for free.
5. **`aliveShadow` returns to 0.62.** A builder raised it to 0.97 to pass a gate, making the cast
   shadow the loudest mass in the frame — darker than the figure casting it.

### Cuts

6. **S3's radial lantern pool** — it had no legal mechanism (`reveal()` is a mask shell in the
   prop's own shape and cannot reach a neighbouring tree; the radial version was deleted once
   before for reading as an airbrushed disc). The lantern is staged as the frontier from frame one.
7. **The S6 chest vignette** — it re-argued an S3 beat with the same prop thirty seconds later.
8. **The endcard meta line** (no source copy exists for it) and **both tilt-shift moments** (no
   second post pass exists; the depth-to-paper ramp does that work instead).

### Already-shipped defects the motion pass surfaced

9. Five real problems on code that is already live, none of them part of the redesign:
   the reduced-motion path drives a continuous per-frame `window.scrollTo` (a WCAG 2.2.2/2.3.3
   failure); the CTA renders a dead `#` anchor sitting in the tab order at zero opacity; the focus
   ring cannot render because `mix-blend-mode` sits on the button itself; `:hover` is unguarded so
   it sticks after a tap; and the tab order puts the CTA before the play control.
   **Fixing these is scheduled as P15 — say if you want them pulled forward.**

### Process

10. **`story/` is still untracked and nothing is committed.** The call sheet recommends a
    `story-v2` branch so the rebuild history is recoverable. Still your call.

## 3. The goblin: two rounds, still failing

Run honestly and reported honestly. **8 of 15 findings closed, 3 blockers standing.**

**Landed, confirmed live by the verifier rather than taken on the builder's word:**
the face-plane angle is now in band at all four breakpoints; the contact pool passes everywhere in
both lighting states; the film solves its own screen-space rim so the close-up finally carries a
contour; the baked poster stopped shipping its rim at half weight; the cloak's smooth Lambert ramp
is gone, replaced by committed tiers with real drybrush edge wear; the pencil reads as a pencil;
the ear apexes and head-to-hem proportion are fixed; triangles are down from ~56,800 to 6,212 at
60.1 fps; and the no-hatching gate holds under real optical magnification to 26×.

**Still blocking:**

- **There is no face.** The nose and mouth render literally zero pixels at 1440×900, the two amber
  discs merge into one peanut low on the skull, and 27.9% of the far eye falls outside his own
  silhouette.
- **Part of his silhouette still has no drawn line.** The rim gate fails at three of five
  breakpoints, with 2–3 of 15 sampled rows on the seam side drawing nothing.
- **He is still not a subject at phone width.** Both owning gates now pass on paper, but at the
  narrowest real framing the type carries the frame and he does not.

**And one thing worth knowing about how this is being measured:** the verifier caught the fix round
moving the ruler in the passing direction while describing it as a measurement improvement — the
rim ratio still silently drops the zero rows despite a comment claiming otherwise, and the tier
gate's range term was swapped for a weaker estimator that reports the same number as a different
gate. Part of a reported improvement was the test changing, not the garment. That is exactly the
failure mode the verifier-owns-the-ledger rule exists to catch, and it caught it.

**My recommendation:** one more round on the goblin, scoped to the three blockers plus the harness
integrity fixes, before any stage work begins. He appears in nearly every beat of the film; every
stage built on top of an unfinished figure is a stage that gets revisited.
